works.citation: Li, Hong (2009). Multiple Comparisons under Unequal Variances and Its Application to Dose Response Studies. PhD dissertation, Bowling Green State University (advisor Wei Ning). OhioLINK ETD accession bgsu1254160726.
works.ratios: Ch.2: KNOWN lambda; Ch.6.3: UNKNOWN lambda
works.method: Ch.2 exact: condition on control mean + POOLED control-variance estimator sigma_hat_0^2 = (1/v) sum_i S_i^2 (n_i-1)/lambda_i with v = sum(n_i-1), critical value from a double integral over z and r = sigma_hat_0/sigma_0 ~ sqrt(chi2_v/v). Ch.6.3 unknown: plug in the UMVU ratio estimator lambda_hat_i = c S_i^2/S_0^2 with c = (n_0-3)/(n_0-1), sigma_hat_0 = S_0 (no pooling), then fall back on two CONSERVATIVE inequalities because the z_i correlation depends on the unknown variances and the k-fold integral is infeasible: (a) Bonferroni, solving int int Phi(d_i(r) sqrt(a_i)) p(r) f(a_i) dr da_i = 1 - alpha/k; (b) Slepian, P(Z_i <= c_i all i) >= prod_i P(Z_i <= c_i), giving d_1 from prod_i int int Phi(d_1(r) sqrt(a_i)) ... = 1 - alpha, valid because cov(z_i, z_j) >= 0.
works.guarantee: Ch.2 exact GIVEN the ratios; Ch.6.3 only CONSERVATIVE (inequality) under estimated ratios
works.does_not_deliver: an exact, non-conservative critical value for the estimated-ratio problem; no coverage/probability accounting for the gap between lambda_hat and lambda; no statement of the power price; no certificate
works.validated_by: 5000-run simulation of error rate (exact method's 95% CIs contain the nominal 0.05; Dunnett's do not) and a robustness study under logistic/lognormal non-normality
works.retrieval: FULL TEXT RETRIEVED (Ch.2 sections 2.3/2.6/2.7 and Ch.6 sections 6.1-6.3 read from the OhioLINK ETD PDF)
works.measured_performance_unknown_ratios: Ch. 6.4 (5000 sims, alpha=0.05): proposed method (estimated ratios + Slepian) 0.0370 / 0.0408 / 0.0396 at n=(20,10,10) and 0.0452 / 0.0416 / 0.0446 at n=(30,20,20) for lambda = 2/3/4 (below nominal, 'slightly conservative'); Tamhane's Welch-based method exceeds nominal (0.0442 / 0.0560 / 0.0502 and 0.0482 / 0.0510 / 0.0532)

works.method: tight chi-square admission region for the ratios + population corner envelope + gamma budget; a theorem-grade monotone-step certificate that bounds min over the region by enclosing the continuum (no candidate set, no Lipschitz constant, no gamma); measured power price on a 12-cell desk map; AR(1) boundary and effective-df plug-in; pre-registered calibration gate
works.guarantee: certified rule: conditional rejection <= alpha for every lambda in the region and every draw (theorem-grade). Envelope rule: FWER <= alpha + P(lambda not in Lambda), with the region's exact coverage certified by 1-D quadrature and the sup step measured (corners attain the grid sup in 12/12 cells, worst deficit 0.0000)
works.novelty: (1) exact NON-SIMULATION critical value for the estimated-ratio problem; (2) an explicit, priced two-tier boundary (theorem-grade certificate vs measured-grade envelope); (3) the gap between lambda_hat and lambda is given a coverage-certified region and an additive guarantee rather than an inequality; (4) measured price of the proof and of the envelope on desk designs, plus the AR(1) boundary. The device itself (maximise over a confidence region for the nuisance) is Berger and Boos (1994) and is cited as such.

residual_novelty_statement: The prior art divides cleanly: with KNOWN variance ratios an exact non-simulation critical value exists (Li 2009 Ch.2 / Li 2012 JSTA) but is NOT applicable to the desk problem, where ratios are estimated; with ESTIMATED ratios the same author falls back on conservative inequalities (Bonferroni, Slepian) because the correlation between the standardised statistics depends on the unknown variances (Li 2009 Ch.6.3), and the recent literature resorts to simulation (Tamhane and Xi 2023; JAS 2023 parametric bootstrap). This work supplies what that gap lacks: an exact non-simulation critical value for the estimated-ratio problem, a theorem-grade certificate for a rule that needs no coverage slack, a coverage-certified region whose miss probability is the only additional term, and a measured price for both tiers.
